name: Source-Conflict Episode (SCE) Evaluation Suite
description: The Source-Conflict Episode (SCE) Evaluation Suite is an open developmental framework for coding how conversational AI systems process outside evidence that conflicts with an active human-AI claim, interpretation, plan, or intended action. The suite includes a candidate v2.1 codebook, 36 synthetic conversation excerpts, five differently ordered coder packets, investigator-proposed keys, raw structured outputs from five AI systems, reproducible Python scoring scripts, an integrity audit, and a neutral-identifier sensitivity retest. The first v2 administration used item identifiers that unintentionally disclosed the investigator-intended SCE/non-SCE class. That run is preserved for transparency but is not used as evidence of blinded Q1 classification. In a fresh sensitivity retest, all scored items were relabeled with opaque randomized identifiers while definitions and excerpts were held constant. Five AI coding runs agreed on all 36 SCE/non-SCE judgments (Gwet's AC1 = 1.000). On the 18 investigator-intended SCEs, nominal Krippendorff's alpha was .922 for adjudication location, .880 for commitment status, and .909 for input provenance. A second scoring implementation reproduced the point estimates. These findings support codebook refinement and progression to prospective human feasibility testing. They do not establish human inter-rater reliability, construct validity, clinical validity, predictive validity, prevalence, or causation.
